thread:
jess: Quick question from oncall: canary flips are noisy when a transient p95 blip hits. Proposing a "handoff delay" between observer candidate and router action (short, token-aware) so we get a confirmation probe before staged split.
kevin: +1. What's the minimal delay we can tolerate without impacting customer safety?
riley: If we keep detection window small (30s) and require confirmation probe within 10s we reduce false positives but still act fast.
jess: Idea: observer emits candidate with score and suggested action. Router samples a confirm probe (1-3 reqs) within 10s. Only on positive confirms do we start staged split.
kevin: Make probes token-aware and per-tenant sampled, otherwise we overwhelm tiny tenants. Also opt-out for private deployments.
ops-bot: Note: runbook must include manual override and audit log for automated escalations.
riley: Also add a suppression TTL (default 12m) after any auto-escalation to avoid flip-flop. Allow immediate re-escalation if score increases by >60%.
jess: Short config sketch for route owners: `auto_fallback: {enabled:true, prefer_quality:true, confirm_probes:2, confirm_window_s:10, suppress_mins:12}`
deploy-bot: rolling test of probe path scheduled at 1767850000. We'll validate sampling and suppression in staging.
kevin: Great. Jess can you draft RFC with probe contract + minimal config + runbook snippets? We'll review in sync on Thu. :thumbsup:
